content.definition: A computational technique that reduces the time complexity of problems involving contiguous subarrays or substrings by maintaining a window of elements and sliding it across the data structure.
when_to_use: Finding optimal subarray/substring with specific properties
When brute force would require nested loops
key_characteristics: Expands and contracts window based on conditions
Processes each element at most twice (once when entering, once when leaving)
Often uses two pointers (left and right boundaries)

fixed_size.example: Maximum sum of k consecutive elements
fixed_size.approach: Slide window by removing leftmost and adding rightmost element

variable_size.description: Window size changes based on conditions
variable_size.approach: Expand window when condition allows, contract when violated

implementation_template.python:
def sliding_window_template(arr, condition):
    left = 0
    result = 0
    window_state = initialize_window_state()
    
    for right in range(len(arr)):
        # Expand window: add arr[right]
        update_window_state(window_state, arr[right])
        
        # Contract window while condition is violated
        while not is_valid(window_state, condition):
            remove_from_window(window_state, arr[left])
            left += 1
        
        # Update result with current valid window
        result = update_result(result, window_state, right - left + 1)
    
    return result

common_patterns.description: Find the optimal window satisfying constraints

common_patterns.name: Fixed Window Sum/Average
examples: Average of subarrays of size k

common_patterns.name: Condition-Based Window
common_patterns.description: Window size varies based on conditions
examples: String with at most k distinct characters

optimization_techniques: Use hash maps for character/element frequency tracking
Maintain running sums instead of recalculating
Use deques for maintaining window extremes
Combine with other techniques like binary search
common_mistakes: Forgetting to update window state when contracting
Not handling edge cases (empty array, single element)
Not resetting window state properly between iterations

complexity_analysis.time: O(n) - each element processed at most twice
complexity_analysis.space: O(k) where k is the size of auxiliary data structures (hash maps, etc.)
complexity_analysis.improvement: Reduces O(n²) or O(n³) brute force to O(n)

interview_tips: Identify if the problem involves contiguous elements
Start with brute force, then optimize with sliding window
Clearly define what constitutes a valid window
Handle edge cases: empty input, single element, no valid window
